findings.title: Tests mock runQuery, so double interpolation of already-interpolated queries is unverified
findings.body: runSplitQuery now interpolates each target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables before building the sub-requests, and those interpolated targets are then handed to datasource.runQuery, which itself performs template-variable interpolation as part of the normal query path. If that second pass is not a no-op on an already-interpolated expression (e.g. a variable value that itself contains `$`, escaped characters, or format-dependent multi-value expansion), the executed query would be double-interpolated and incorrect. All new tests ('Interpolates queries before execution' in both querySplitting.test.ts and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts) replace runQuery with a jest mock, so they only assert that the pre-interpolation happened and cannot detect that the real runQuery interpolates again. A test that spies on the real interpolation path (or a check that runQuery skips interpolation) is needed before this can be trusted.

findings.title: $__range guard in querySupportsSplitting now runs against the interpolated expression
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting explicitly refuses to split queries containing a range variable because $__range must be interpolated on the backend against the split time range. This PR changes the order so that datasource.applyTemplateVariables runs before the partition into splitting/non-splitting queries (line 299 precedes the partition on line 300). The guard isQueryWithRangeVariable now inspects the interpolated expr: in any context where the frontend template service resolves $__range (for example when scopedVars carries a range variable, or via a dashboard variable whose value is '$__range'), the literal '$__range' no longer appears in the expr, the query is misclassified as splittable, and it gets executed with a per-chunk $__range baked in from the wrong (already-replaced) range, producing wrong data. Previously the check ran on the raw expression. The guard should be evaluated on the pre-interpolation expression, or interpolation must demonstrably preserve $__range.
